Widespread rainfall over much of western and central North Dakota led to significant drought improvement. During the first week of June, most locations with a drought designation saw a one-category improvement in drought intensity. By mid-June, almost all locations were designated D1 (Moderate Drought) or better. Only a tiny sliver of very far western Golden Valley County remained in D2 (severe drought) designation, with the mass majority of the county in D1.

Severe to extreme drought conditions, D2-D3, continued into the month of May over much of western into parts of central North Dakota. Very limited changes occurred through mid-May, but widespread rains over central into parts of western North Dakota led to some improvement. The most notable improvement was to the eastern portions of the drought area where heavier rains occurred, with Adams, Hettinger, and Mercer Counties improving from D2 (Severe Drought) to D1 (Moderate Drought).

Severe to extreme drought conditions, D2-D3, continued through the month of April over much of western into parts of central North Dakota. A few changes did occur during the month. In early April, Grant County improved from D2 (severe drought) to D1 (moderate drought), and D2 conditions spread through most of Mercer County. In late April Williams, Divide, Burke, and Renville Counties improved from D2 to D1.

Along Highway 83, fifteen power poles were broken or significantly damaged on both sides of the highway.
